# v1.1.0-dev.68 — The last two off the list

Pre-release off the `dev` branch. Builds on `v1.1.0-dev.67`.

Both things dev.67 left open. Neither needed rushing after all.

## A Saved Size Your Display Can't Do Now Looks Different

Pick a resolution, save the profile, then plug in a monitor that
can't do it. WLM keeps the setting and applies it the moment the
display starts offering it, which is the right behaviour.

It just looked identical to a size you'd typed a second ago. The
only thing telling them apart was a sentence underneath.

The row carries its own mark now:

```
Landscape   3440 × 1440   @ 100 Hz   [ NOT OFFERED YET ]
```

It's driven by the same check the sentence uses, which is what stops
the two disagreeing. It stays out of the way while you're picking
from the list. It doesn't appear while you're still typing a number.

## Slot Position Doesn't Prove Ownership

Parsec's driver takes custom resolutions in five numbered slots.
Parsec claims three of them for your client's screen sizes and WLM
writes the other two. Nothing in there records who wrote what.
Position was the only signal.

There's a well-known Parsec companion tool that renumbers those
slots when it saves: it reads them, skips the empty ones, and
writes what's left back starting from the first. On a machine where
your two slots are empty, one press of its save button slides
Parsec's own resolutions into them.

After that, WLM would have shown you Parsec's resolutions and
called them yours.

Registering now remembers the sizes it wrote, not just how many,
and checks them when it reads the slots back. If something doesn't
match, it says so and suggests looking before you register over it.

If there's nothing to compare against, on a fresh install or after
clearing settings, it stays quiet. Not knowing isn't the same as
knowing something's wrong. A warning that cries wolf stops being read.

## One For The Changelog

Writing the test for that check turned up a bug in it, and in the
registration read-back shipped last release. Both asked whether a
slot's numbers were real by converting them and checking the result
was finite. Converting an empty value gives you zero. Zero is
perfectly finite.

So a slot with a missing value was being read as a genuine 0 × 0
resolution and reported as somebody else's handiwork. Both now
reject empty values before converting.

## Install

Auto-updates from dev.53 and later. Otherwise unzip and run.
